accepted.s: N.G. Ranga is associated with which of the following titles?
accepted.x: N.G. Ranga was popularly known as Rythu Bandhu. He was also described as the Father of the Indian Peasant Movement and as Acharya.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the popular title associated with a peasant leader.
accepted.sec: Pioneers and leaders of the Kisan movement → popular titles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding N.G. Ranga is correct?
o: He founded the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham alone in 1915.
He was known as the Father of the Indian Peasant Movement.
He led the 1937 Rythu Yatra as a village association organiser.
accepted.x: N.G. Ranga was known as the Father of the Indian Peasant Movement. The Munagala Award was authored by Gottipati Brahmaiah, while the 1937 Rythu Yatra was led by Kommareddi Satyanarayana.
accepted.tq: Use the leader–title association and reject swapped deeds.
accepted.sec: Pioneers and leaders of the Kisan movement → popular titles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. N.G. Ranga was also known as Acharya.
2. He received the Padma Vibhushan in 1991.
3. He founded the Andhra Kisan movement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. N.G. Ranga was known as Acharya, received the Padma Vibhushan in 1991, and founded the Andhra Kisan movement.
accepted.tq: Check each biographical statement independently before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Pioneers and leaders of the Kisan movement → popular titles

accepted.s: Who among the following authored the Munagala Award?
accepted.x: Gottipati Brahmaiah authored the Munagala Award. He was also a pioneer of the zamindari ryot movement and Secretary of the APCC.
accepted.tq: Match the named document with its author, guarding against swapped deeds.
accepted.sec: Pioneers and leaders of the Kisan movement → popular titles

accepted.s:
Kommareddi Satyanarayana is associated with which of the following activities?

1. Formation of village peasant associations in 1935
2. Leadership of the 1937 Rythu Yatra
3. Presidency of the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Kommareddi Satyanarayana formed village peasant associations in 1935 and led the 1937 Rythu Yatra. The 1936 AIKS President was Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.
accepted.tq: Separate a leader’s documented activities from a similar organisational position.
accepted.sec: Pioneers and leaders of the Kisan movement → popular titles

accepted.s:

3. Gottipati Brahmaiah — Srikakulam kisan leader

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao and Gouthu Latchanna were Srikakulam kisan leaders. Gottipati Brahmaiah is associated with the zamindari ryot movement and the Munagala Award.
accepted.tq: Use the regional association to eliminate the swapped leader.
accepted.sec: Pioneers and leaders of the Kisan movement → popular titles

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a book associated with N.G. Ranga?
accepted.x: Credo of World Peasantry, Revolutionary Peasantry and Fight for Freedom are books associated with N.G. Ranga. The Munagala Award was authored by Gottipati Brahmaiah and is not a book of Ranga.

accepted.s: The First Agricultural Labourers’ Mahasabha associated with N.G. Ranga was founded at:

accepted.s: Which one of the following was India’s first Kisan School?
accepted.x: The Peasant Institute, or Ramanayidu Rythu Vidyalayam, at Nidubrolu was India’s first Kisan School. It was established in 1933–34 with Bharathi Devi and Ranga’s brothers.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first institution from later schools and political centres.
accepted.sec: N.G. Ranga - kisan institutions founded → place + year

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Political summer school — Kothapatnam — 1937
2. Rajakeeya Pathashala — Kankipadu — 1939
3. Andhra Rythu Vidyalayam — Madanapalle — May 1938

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. The Political Summer School was at Kothapatnam in 1937, Rajakeeya Pathashala at Kankipadu in 1939, and Andhra Rythu Vidyalayam at Madanapalle in May 1938.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure place–year pairs and verify the complete set.
accepted.sec: N.G. Ranga - kisan institutions founded → place + year

accepted.s: The Peasant Institute at Nidubrolu, also called Ramanayidu Rythu Vidyalayam, was established during:
accepted.x: The Peasant Institute or Ramanayidu Rythu Vidyalayam was established at Nidubrolu in 1933–34 and was regarded as India’s first Kisan School.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely spaced institutional years.
accepted.sec: N.G. Ranga - kisan institutions founded → place + year

accepted.s:
With reference to the All India Kisan Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. It was founded in April 1936 at Lucknow.
2. Its founding took place during an INC session.
3. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was its President and N.G. Ranga was its Secretary.
4. The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham merged into it in 1940.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham merged into the AIKS in 1936, not 1940.
accepted.tq: Reject the famous-word year trap in an otherwise correct organisational statement.
accepted.sec: All India Kisan Sabha and kisan events → year

accepted.s: The Palasa session of the All India Kisan Sabha was held in:
accepted.x: The Palasa AIKS session was held in March 1940 and was presided over by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.
accepted.tq: Separate a session date from the organisation’s founding date.
accepted.sec: All India Kisan Sabha and kisan events → year

accepted.s: Which one of the following events occurred immediately after the Palasa AIKS session of March 1940?
o: The founding of the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham
The founding of the First Agricultural Labourers’ Mahasabha
accepted.x: The Mandasa firing followed the Palasa AIKS session and took place on 1 April 1940.
accepted.tq: Use the immediate chronological link between a conference and its reported consequence.
accepted.sec: All India Kisan Sabha and kisan events → year

accepted.s: Why was N.G. Ranga jailed in connection with the Palasa AIKS session?
o: He occupied the zamindar’s surplus land.
He defied an order while confined to Nidubrolu.
He refused to preside over the session.
accepted.x: N.G. Ranga was confined to Nidubrolu, defied the order, and was consequently jailed in connection with the Palasa session.
accepted.tq: Identify the action that explains the stated consequence.
accepted.sec: All India Kisan Sabha and kisan events → year

accepted.s: During the Second World War, the communist-led All India Kisan Sabha supported which policy?
accepted.x: During the Second World War, the communist-led AIKS supported the policy known as the People’s War.
accepted.tq: Match the organisation with its wartime political position.
accepted.sec: All India Kisan Sabha and kisan events → year

accepted.s: Which organisation was founded by N.G. Ranga in 1943 after he left the All India Kisan Sabha?
accepted.x: N.G. Ranga left the AIKS during the wartime period and founded the Andhra Rashtra Kisan Congress in 1943.
accepted.tq: Use the organisational succession to distinguish similarly named bodies.
accepted.sec: All India Kisan Sabha and kisan events → year

accepted.s: Munagala paragana was situated in which administrative area at the time of the struggle?
accepted.x: Munagala paragana was located in Nandigama taluk of Krishna district at the time. It is now associated with Suryapet/Nalgonda.

o: Nanduri Prasada Rao and Uppala Ramayya
Immadi Papayya and Kodati Venkata Narasimha Rao
Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya
accepted.x: The Munagala Zamindari Rythu Sangham was founded in 1930 by Immadi Papayya, Kodati Venkata Narasimha Rao and others.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kalukova Satyagraha:
1. It took place in 1938.
2. It was led by Nanduri Prasada Rao.
3. It concerned a paddy wage of 80 seers per acre.
4. The Sub-Collector made the zamindar pay.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The 1938 Kalukova Satyagraha was led by Nanduri Prasada Rao over the 80-seers-per-acre paddy wage, and the Sub-Collector compelled the zamindar to pay.
accepted.tq: Verify the date, leader, demand and administrative outcome as one event cluster.
accepted.sec: Munagala paragana struggle - district, zamindar, leaders, outcome

accepted.s: The Brahmaiah Award in the Munagala struggle was issued on:
accepted.x: Gottipati Brahmaiah mediated the settlement and issued the Brahmaiah Award on 15 January 1939. It covered 142 villages.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the award date from the later Munagala Day and withdrawal date.
accepted.sec: Munagala paragana struggle - district, zamindar, leaders, outcome

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Munagala struggle?
o: Uppala Ramayya led land occupations, and 350 women were lathi-charged.
The struggle ended with the 1938 Kalukova wage settlement alone.
The Brahmaiah Award was accepted permanently by the zamindar.
The zamindari was abolished on 11 June 1939.
accepted.x: The Brahmaiah Award was broken, after which Uppala Ramayya led land occupations and 350 women were lathi-charged. The zamindari struggle was later withdrawn on 19 June 1939 after assurances by Prakasam and Ranga.
accepted.tq: Reject the overstatement and identify the documented consequence of the broken award.
accepted.sec: Munagala paragana struggle - district, zamindar, leaders, outcome

accepted.s: Munagala Day was observed on:
accepted.x: Munagala Day was observed on 11 June 1939. The struggle was withdrawn on 19 June 1939 after Prakasam and N.G. Ranga promised action.
accepted.tq: Separate two closely related dates in the same movement.
accepted.sec: Munagala paragana struggle - district, zamindar, leaders, outcome

accepted.s: The Challapalli zamindari struggle began with the revolt of farmers in Potharlanka, Ghantasala and Movva in:
accepted.x: Farmers in Potharlanka, Ghantasala and Movva revolted in June 1930 under the leadership of Gorrepati Venkata Subbayya.
accepted.tq: Link the opening event of a struggle with its exact year and leader.
accepted.sec: Challapalli zamindari struggle → leaders + year

accepted.s:
Which of the following events is correctly matched with the Challapalli zamindari struggle?

1. 1939 — The zamindar grabbed 600 acres of temple land.
2. 1942 — Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya led the struggle.
3. 1946 — Firing over Kishkindapalem land killed four persons.
4. July 1947 — Farmers occupied the zamindar’s surplus land.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya were jailed in 1942, while the 1946 firing killed four persons and farmers occupied surplus land in July 1947.
accepted.tq: Track the sequence of events and test every year–event pair.
accepted.sec: Challapalli zamindari struggle → leaders + year

accepted.s: The Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra was launched by N.G. Ranga on:
accepted.x: N.G. Ranga launched the Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra on 3 July 1937. Kommareddi Satyanarayana led the yatra.

accepted.s: The Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra was compared to which national movement?
accepted.x: The Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra was compared to the Dandi March. It ended with a memorandum submitted to Speaker Bulusu Sambamurthy.

accepted.sec: Kisan marches and ryot conferences → venue + year

accepted.s: Who led the Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra after it was launched by N.G. Ranga?

accepted.s:
Who among the following were the founders of the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham?

1. N.G. Ranga
2. Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana
3. Maganti Bapineedu
4. B.V. Ratnam

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: N.G. Ranga, Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana and Maganti Bapineedu founded the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham. B.V. Ratnam was its first General Secretary, not a listed founder.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham is correct?
o: It was based at Palasa and merged into the AIKS in 1940.
It was based at Lucknow and was founded by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.
It was based at Nidubrolu, with B.V. Ratnam as first President.
It was based at Vijayawada, with N.G. Ranga as first President and B.V. Ratnam as first General Secretary.
accepted.x: The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham was based at Vijayawada. N.G. Ranga was its first President and B.V. Ratnam its first General Secretary; it merged into the AIKS in 1936.
accepted.tq: Test headquarters and office-bearers together, guarding against organisational swaps.
